title: Kojima Productions' survival story may sound strikingly familiar to struggling devs
text:
Even celebrated auteurs have to pay bank loans on time.
The dust continues to settle on the fallout from Sony Interactive Entertainment's sudden decision to end funding and publishing support for Kojima Productions' Physint , which sent studio founder Hideo Kojima on a three-month race to find new business partners who could fund and publish his spiritual successor to the Metal Gear Solid series—ultimately landing a deal with Microsoft-owned Xbox.
Now in an interview with IGN , Kojima has shared some details about that scramble for funds that seem strikingly similar to many other stories we've heard of developers searching for funding. These common traits show that the financial headwinds and strategic missteps driving the still-rolling video game industry contraction can send celebrity developers and more modest studio heads seeking the same solutions (though the former group has an outsized advantage when it comes to convincing investors of their audience appeal).
Related: 'We want to keep it very simple:' How Nex Playground is beating expectations during a hardware crisis
Kojima told IGN that his funding race began after a Zoom call with unnamed PlayStation representatives where he was told they "can no longer fund development for Physint ." The news apparently shocked him so much that he said his mind went "blank" to the point that he struggles to remember details from the call. What he does recall is that he immediately worried about the financial health of Kojima Productions—which had staffed up to work on two projects: OD and Physint .
"I hire according to how many projects we have, and we have two," he told IGN. "If we lose one contract, I thought I might have to cut all the people working on Physint, right? Or our studio could end up collapsing because we'll run out of cashflow." A few days after Sony delivered the news, Kojima Productions moved some Physint developers onto the OD team and informed them of the search for a new partner. The company has not had to lay off any employees.
It was here he became candid about another loan fueling Kojima Productions: a bank loan. Kojima didn't go into details, but he indicated that sometime after Death Stranding released, he was able to secure a loan from an unnamed bank to bring funding into Kojima Productions. "If they find out that a project has been stopped or canceled, we'd be in big trouble," he said in reference to that.
This led to Kojima, along with company president Shinji Hirano and head of talent Aki Saito scrambling to strategize how they would seek out new partnerships. He said he decided to pitch Physint to new partners not just as a project in search of funding but as a new intellectual property that might attract support from film, TV, and streaming producers.
Related: Escape From Tarkov dev wants to bet on 'risky' games with its new publishing arm
Said funding conversations apparently did not cover other "support" that Kojima Productions needed, such as technical support, marketing support, organized playtesting, and other duties a publisher like PlayStation would have wrangled. Kojima said it was these considerations that sent him to Xbox, who apparently shared his fervor for developing an original property that would go beyond video games.
Developers everywhere are scrambling for funding
The remainder of Kojima's conversation with IGN concerned his relationship with Sony and PlayStation (eventually leading the studio to put out a statement pushing back against a report from Bloomberg News concerning that dynamic), but the stakes of this drama ripple far beyond these three companies and speak to a struggle facing developers everywhere.
Developers racing to save games after the sudden exit of funding partners is a familiar tale in the game industry—but it's taken on new urgency in the last few years as rolling layoffs , high-profile underperforming games , and uncertain economic conditions driven by AI-driven memory shortages and other world events . This has led some publishers and game funders to pull out of signed deals before games even ship.
Related: Xbox continues 'reset' with Halo Studios layoffs and Undead Labs divestment
In fact, Xbox—Kojima's new financial partner—is one such party that's sent developers scrambling to save their studios. Earlier this year it spun off four subsidiary studios while beginning the process of laying off 3,200 employees. It also pulled support for IO Interactive's unnamed fantasy game, echoing its decision in 2025 to do the same for Avalanche Studios' Contraband . The developers of The Initiative's Perfect Dark reboot apparently launched a similar race for survival similar to Kojima Productions' in 2025 after the studio was shut down, seeking to restart development at Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics.
Unlike Kojima, that team wasn't able to secure such a deal.

title: Sony appears to censor LGBTQ content in Marvel's Wolverine for some regions
text:
A mutant marriage goes unmentioned in some parts of the world.
Insomniac Games' and Sony Interactive Entertainment's new comic book-inspired blockbuster game Marvel's Wolverine appears to have had LGBTQ content censored from the game for users in certain regions of the world. Reports of this removal come from a number of users on X and Reddit (and were spotted by Kotaku ), who all noticed that content referring to the marriage of two non-playable female characters named Mystique and Tyger has been scrubbed from the game.
One video from Reddit user Squeakyyy appears to capture all of the censored content referring to Mystique and Tyger's marriage. These include an in-game photo of their wedding day and voice lines where each refers to the other as their wife, or that they love each other. The photo in question is blurred out when the player picks it up from Mystique's locker, and the audio simply cuts out when Mystique or Tyger says the censored words. The subtitles for these lines are replaced by asterisk marks.
Related: Bungie declares it's 'not done with Destiny' as it lays out studio's future
The user's post describes this censorship as taking place in "Middle East versions" of the game, but it's unclear as of this writing if this ban is in effect in every Middle Eastern country or if it's been implemented in other regions.
This wouldn't be the first time that Insomniac's Marvel-themed games have been modified to remove LGBTQ-themed content when being distributed in the Middle East. Sony previously altered some content from 2023's Marvel's Spider-Man 2 , including the display of pride flags and a side quest featuring a gay couple, when releasing the game in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. Depictions of homosexuality are censored in both countries , with homosexuality and other types of LGBTQ identity also being outlawed.
Such censorship is sadly not limited to one region. Companies like EA and Roblox Corporation have previously wrangled with the difficulty of releasing content in countries like Russia, which also outlaws homosexuality.
Game Developer has reached out to PlayStation for comment on this story and will update it upon the company's response.

title: Bungie declares it's 'not done with Destiny' as it lays out studio's future
text:
'Destiny is foundational to Bungie's future.'
A surprise update from Destiny 2 and Marathon developer Bungie has given the video game industry a reason to turn its head at the Sony-owned subsidiary. The company revealed an unexpected bit of news in a new update from studio head Poria Torkan and Marathon general manager Josh Deane: that it is returning to development on the Destiny series and preparing to "unvault" years of archived content for Destiny 2.
"Destiny is foundational to Bungie's future," the studio declared in a blog post penned by the two studio higher-ups. "We have more stories to tell, new worlds to build, but we have to do it right and give our teams the time they need to do justice to this amazing universe."
"We want to return Destiny to its original promise, to recapture the qualities that have always made it special. The awe-inspiring mystery, meaningful discovery, and a community of Guardians coming together against impossible odds. That begins with restoring important parts of Destiny 2’s history that players can no longer experience today."
Related: Sony appears to censor LGBTQ content in Marvel's Wolverine for some regions
Developers and other industry professionals might be surprised to hear such a proclamation given that Bungie declared Destiny 2 active development would be ending in June 2026. Shortly thereafter, it laid off almost 300 employees working on the long-running game. Torkan acknowledged these and other turbulent events in a video accompanying the post, saying that "we have lost trust, lost incredible colleagues, and our ambitions as a studio stalled."
"We chased vision without enough focus on what players loved and that's on us. We own that."
The process of rebuilding that trust apparently begins with restoring years of "vaulted" Destiny 2 content. For years, Bungie would cycle playable expansions in and out of Destiny 2 through a process it called "vaulting," meaning a significant chunk of the game's older content was unplayable by the public. This process created some legal headaches for Bungie as it recently fended off a ( now-settled ) lawsuit accusing the company of plagiarism in one of its vaulted campaigns.
Making said content playable again isn't simply a matter of pushing a button. Torkan and Deane noted that recent expansions to Destiny 2 overhauled elements such as the games' lighting, combat, and other "underlying systems." "This restoration is the first step to lay the foundation for how we reforge into new stories and games that you all deserve," they wrote.
Bungie intends to be more than a Marathon studio
After previously signaling that the studio intends to significantly overhaul Marathon , Bungie is now saying that the game "did not reach as many players" as the studio hoped for, and that it understands the game "needs to evolve." It was lighter on the specifics of this evolution, only saying that the game's developers will "continue strengthening its combat, world, and competitive tension while giving players more agency in how they engage with the game."
Related: Microsoft raises price of Xbox consoles once again, sunsets 2TB model
It's unknown if either a Destiny revival or major updates to Marathon would see the company hiring back any laid-off developers, many of whom might have experience with both games' underlying systems.
With Marathon missing major metrics, Sony previously declaring that Destiny 2 underperformed since its 2021 purchase of Bungie, and wave after wave of layoffs, the studio that once forged to Xbox's Halo series has certainly been going through hard times. Torkan and Deane acknowledged these difficulties in the post, saying that its future "depends on making clear choices about where we focus, delivering what we say we will, and being honest about our successes and our failures."
"Stability doesn't mean shrinking our ambition. I just means we have to focus on the things you want to see from us, and making sure our vision matches our reality," they wrote. Alongside improvements to the Destiny series and Marathon , the pair promised that the company inends to "increase transparency around development priorities" and "communicate more consistently, especially when plans change."
Related: Grand Theft Auto 6's $80 price settles the $100 question
Torkan and Deane's message was largely directed toward players, but their final words offered some sense about what is being communicated to workers inside Bungie. "We’ve made several changes with how we operate by simplifying our priorities, reducing competing initiatives, moving decisions closer to the teams building our games, and changing how we measure success to place greater emphasis on player satisfaction," they concluded.
"There is still a great deal of work ahead and challenges to overcome, but we believe deeply in this studio, our people, and the games we are building. But belief is not enough. It’s on us to prove progress through what we deliver. "

title: 'Do not': Rockstar outlines modding rules before GTA VI touches down
text:
Official Rockstar storylines, characters, and other elements from the studio's 'established continuity' are off-limits.
Rockstar has restated its modding guidelines with the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI looming large, and the words "do not" appear in abundance.
Although the studio has yet to confirm a launch date for GTA VI on PC, it is being proactive about laying down the law for those who might want to tinker with the title when the time comes. The guidelines will also apply to existing releases such as GTA V and Red Dead Redemption II, both of which have well-established modding and roleplaying communities.
The rulebook was shared by Rockstar on September 10, 2026, and prohibits modders from creating content that combines maps, locations, characters, storylines, in-game assets, or other IP from one Rockstar title into another.
Notably, they also seek to prevent people from expanding or modifying official Rockstar storylines, plots, missions, characters, or other elements from the studio's "established continuity."
Related: King workers call strike after collective agreement negotiations stall
Multiplayer modding has been restricted to Rockstar's official licensed Creator Platform—unless the studio has stated otherwise. Any creations that infringe on Rockstar Games' own or third-party IP and services are off-limits, too.
"Do not use protected elements of anyone else's intellectual property in your mod, including art, characters, music, photos, games, advertisements, brands or logos, real-world locations, etc," read the guidelines. "Do not modify or reuse voiceover performances from any game released by Rockstar Games. Do not use any real-world person's voice, image, or likeness without written permission."
In addition, would-be modders have been warned to avoid implementing "unauthorized or abusive monetization" systems. Rockstar has stressed that people must only monetize their mods via its own official Creator Platform.
"You may only monetize your mods via digital storefront providers approved by Rockstar Games and in compliance with all applicable laws, rules, and policies," states the company.
"We do not permit mods to enable real money gambling, 'loot boxes,' 'gacha,' or similar chance mechanics for real money. We do not permit the offering or selling of in-game virtual currency for real money. We do not permit the use or promotion of cryptocurrency or crypto assets (e.g., 'NFTs,' tokens, memecoin, or stablecoin)."
The full modding guidelines are available on the Rockstar Games website .

title: Xbox continues 'reset' with Halo Studios layoffs and Undead Labs divestment
text:
Activision is developing the next Halo title, and Ninja Theory is being shuttered.
Xbox has laid off another 268 employees as part of a major reset it commenced in July 2026. At the time, the company said it would be cutting 3,200 roles before the end of the fiscal year, starting with 1,600 layoffs across major studios such as Obsidian, Zenimax Online Studios, and id Software.
Now, in a statement shared with Xbox employees ( republished on Xbox Wire ), division chief content officer Matt Booty has confirmed another 268 workers have been jettisoned from the U.S. conglomerate.
The latest redundancies include workers at Halo Studios, other first-party teams, and the Xbox Game Studios management and central functions layer. Booty said the division is now "roughly three-quarter of the way through [our] previously announced restructuring."
"I am deeply grateful for what our colleagues have built, and I know how difficult today will be for those leaving and the teams around them," he added.
Related: 'We want to keep it very simple:' How Nex Playground is beating expectations during a hardware crisis
In July, Xbox divested Psychonauts maker Double Fine and South of Midnight developer Compulsion Games. Notably, it confirmed it was in similar talks with Undead Labs, Ninja Theory, and Arkane.
Today, Booty explained Undead Labs has "successfully transitioned" out of Xbox on similar terms to Double Fine, which managed to retain its IP, back catalog, and runway funding.
"Undead Labs has now successfully transitioned on similar terms and, with a new publisher, will release State of Decay 3 day one on Game Pass," said Booty.
Ninja Theory, however, is facing closure after two separate agreements for the Senua developer collapsed. "We will now begin consultation with employees on a proposed closure while continuing to explore other paths forward," Booty continued, before noting that Xbox remains in a lengthy consultation with Arkane.
Xbox is also moving to merge a number of internal studios in a bid to shrink its operating footprint and focus its publishing efforts.
As a result, Call of Duty maker Activision— acquired by Xbox in 2023 for almost $70 billion —is expanding its remit and is now developing the next Halo title led by a "new, purpose-built team." A small Halo Studios contingent will continue supporting Halo products in-market. Internal Xbox studios Rare and World's Edge have also been moved under the Activision umbrella.
Bethesda will now house Obsidian, which will continue working on current projects such as Grounded and an upcoming Fallout title made in collaboration with Bethesda Game Studios.
King will expand to include Microsoft Casual Games. Booty claimed that move will unite "two global leaders" in casual game design and live operations.
Related: Escape From Tarkov dev wants to bet on 'risky' games with its new publishing arm
Finally, Fable developer Playground Games and Forza custodian Turn 10 will be merged into a single studio focused on those two franchises. "These two studios have been creative and franchise partners for over a decade, and today’s changes will formally move their work into one team," added Booty.
An email sent to Blizzard employees by a senior leader (viewed by Game Developer) indicates the World of Warcraft maker is not impacted by "today's announcements." Although, that careful phrasing doesn't rule out cuts in the future. An Xbox representative has confirmed the legitimacy of that email.
In July, Xbox workers told Game Developer that Microsoft's decision to make five rounds of mass layoffs in just three years will hamstring a number of internal studios due to a cataclysmic loss of talent. Those impacted by the cuts also accused the company of failing to treat employees with dignity and respect.

title: Escape From Tarkov dev wants to bet on 'risky' games with its new publishing arm
text:
Battlestate Games Publishing aims to provide publishing support to 'hardcore' games.
Battlestate Games Publishing, the recently announced publishing arm by Escape from Tarkov developer Battlestate Games, is seeking to provide support to "hardcore" and "risky" projects.
After announcing its new publishing venture at the beginning of September , Battlestate Games spoke to PCGamesN to provide more context about its plans, which are bolstered by a desire to "help hardcore FPS and niche games" like Escape from Tarkov , the company's COO Nikita Buyanov says.
"We thought: 'why not? We'll give it a shot.' It's not like we can do it in one single step—like just start publishing projects and all of that. We will need a lot of time, and it will be a new experience for us, too," Buyanov tells the publication.
The COO adds that the company isn't treating the arm as a "big publishing business," but rather as a helping hand for small, indie, and niche projects, which he generalizes as hardcore games.
Related: 'We want to keep it very simple:' How Nex Playground is beating expectations during a hardware crisis
"We will allow them to use our audience, and our legacy even, to break through—to have something new, and to [generate] some kind of interest in the hardcore community. We don't treat it as a big, upscaled marketing and all of that. It's more or less an experiment for us, and for the whole industry to make a centralized platform for these kinds of games."
This year alone, the developers behind the likes of Journey and Peak have launched publishing labels, using their established commercial successes to bolster other developers and pay it forward, either by providing funds or by acting as full-service publishers.
Buyanov says the publishing arm has already received more than 100 pitches. There's "maybe five to ten games which are already suitable" for what the studio is looking for. Yet, it still has to decide on what it needs to provide support, and how exactly to start doing so.
The COO is bullish on the idea that Battlestate Games isn't targeting a financial approach to publishing, and rather, it just wants to see and test "risky" games.
"Some risky ideas with risky implementation—some prototypes even—are going to have something in there, like the scent of greatness; something special in there that can be unfolded into something new. So this is our approach: really risky, interesting ideas above potential profits and all that," he says.

title: 'We want to keep it very simple:' How Nex Playground is beating expectations during a hardware crisis
text:
'If we don't create margin we can't continue to invest in software, and our software costs are going up every year—significantly.'
We're not quite at the finish line, but 2026 has already been a huge year for Nex Playground. The family-focused, motion-controlled console is well on the way to becoming a global platform after expanding beyond the United States. The device has already touched down in Canada, the United Kingdom and Germany—while Asia is slowly coming into focus.
Nex, the company behind the active play system, also secured $150 million in equity and debt financing to accelerate that worldwide rollout. Meanwhile, the platform's rolling roster of titles (accessible via an annual or quarterly subscription plan) has been bolstered with the addition of notable licensed projects like Sonic Forces and Pac-Man .
In May this year, Nex Playground head of international Tom Kang said the company has ambitions " as big as the Wii ." It's a bold claim when you consider Nintendo's system sold over 101 million units worldwide, but the company is standing by those words. During a follow-up conversation at Gamescom 2026, Kang told Game Developer the Nex Playground continues to exceed expectations.
Related: Escape From Tarkov dev wants to bet on 'risky' games with its new publishing arm
Discussing how the device has fared in the UK, Kang said sales velocity is currently beating internal weekly and monthly targets. According to Kang, delivering an omni-channel launch across retail stories and digital platforms like TikTok Shop has been fundamental to that success.
"We've learned omni-channel works. That being where customers are means we're able to create awareness and conversion. We're learning that TikTok is serving multiple functions as a discovery channel and a funneling channel, meaning people discover it there and buy it there or somewhere else," says Kang. "Creators also love creating content for the Playground because it shows well. You know, seeing is believing right? That's why we have demos that are playable at retails store, right?"
Establishing a solid supply chain in the middle of an AI-driven component crisis (that has already resulted in price hikes for the Nex Playground) has been a critical challenge for the company, but Kang is confident Nex has the solution. "We have a new leader who's managing global supply and we're way more nimble than we used to be. We're now making product in more than one region—so we're making hardware in Mexico as well as China—and so we have a shorter lead time to get product to different global regions. Also, the local distributor partners are playing a big role," says Kang.
He explains Nex initially raised hardware pricing in response to the tariffs imposed by the U.S. administration, which have since been deemed illegal by the U.S. Supreme Court . Still, he accepts the component crisis has thrown the consumer electronic market into chaos, but stressed that Nex remains committed to selling hardware that is "as affordable as possible."
Related: Xbox continues 'reset' with Halo Studios layoffs and Undead Labs divestment
"We absorb so much of [the cost] to this day to get to this point, versus our peers," Kang continues. "We have an internal mantra that we have to have margins for both hardware and software, even if they're slim. We want to be a sustainable business. If we don't create margin we can't continue to invest in software, and our software costs are going up every year—significantly. We were profitable last year as a company and we're likely going to be [profitable] this year as well. So we're managing that mix well."
"Our current mode says that under the current cost structure we have a sustainable business that can generate annual profits. Our business, because the backend is driven by subscriptions, the more [hardware] units are out there, the more the economics get better for us."
When asked whether Nex will increase the price of its Play Pass subscriptions as the market evolves, Kang said the company will likely assess those on a "biannual basis" but doesn't expect significant change in the near future. "Content drives this device and we want to continue to invest in it," he adds.
Related: Kojima Productions' survival story may sound strikingly familiar to struggling devs
"Subscription fatigue is a phrase [we hear], but we're delivering subscription value"
On the subject of software, Kang claims that "almost every game publisher" in the industry has approached Nex about a collaboration. He says those publishers are especially interested in reviving legacy Kinect titles— such as Freefall Racers , which originally launched in 2013 for the Kinect and was recently given a new lease of life on Nex Playground.
Porting those titles over to a modern-day platform isn't straightforward, mind, but Kang said Nex is committed to the cause. " Freefall Racers was built in Unreal. Our tech stack is built on Unity. So, it was essentially a full port over to a new game engine so [the process] wasn't trivial. Then also we optimized gameplay so it's a little more friendly for younger audiences. Almost in no instance is it a direct port. But that lane is super, super important to us."
Given Nex seems intent on revisiting some of the motion controlled classics of yesteryear, we ask whether there's a chance we might see a few EyeToy titles make an appearance on the platform. Kang isn't ruling anything out. "We're going to look at a lot of those opportunities," he replies.
As that software catalog widens, Nex must be smart about how it manages its portfolio to keep users engaged. The Nex Playground only has 64 gigabytes of memory, so there is no way for owners to download every single game available on the system. By way of a solution, the device will automatically offload titles that aren't generating playtime. Though, it'll be possible to manually redownload them with a few button clicks.
Discussing how Nex's subscription offering might evolve in the future, Kang is quick to rule out the addition of advertisements. "We really think that detracts from the experience," he adds. "We want to keep it very simple both from a subscription standpoint and no ads. We don't want kids going to their parents saying 'buy me this game,' and we don't want selling to children to be one of the things that promoted on the platform."
Kang says Nex's subscription model is currently bang on the money. The proof, he claims, is a global attach rate of over 80 percent. During an era where the phase 'subscription fatigue' is becoming well worn, Kang feels Nex is delivering "extreme value" to its customers by focusing on serving families first.
"I'm a parent who raised two kids," says Kang. "If there's a closet in my house and you open it, there are literally hundreds of board games in there. If you go in our bedroom, my son has made every Star Wars Lego set in existence. If you count the dollars I spent on those, it's in the thousands. We're charging like €99 per year. We're launching a game per month. Not only are we doing that, but we're updating with live content. Subscription fatigue is a phrase [we hear], but we're delivering subscription value because every day the value of the subscription gets greater."
Game Developer attended Gamescom as a media ambassador. Flights and accommodation were covered by event organizers.

title: Hipster Whale could revive or reimagine a range of retro classics after Atari acquisition
text:
Crossy Road maker Hipster Whale is busy delving into the Atari IP archives following its acquisition by the rejuvenated retro label.
The buyout marks a turning point for the (formerly) independent Australian studio 14 years after after its breakout hit Crossy Road, which has amassed over 340m downloads since launch.
At its peak, Crossy Road was generating $250k per day in revenue, and it made Hipster Whale $10m within 90 days of release back in 2014, cofounder Matt Hall tells us.
Crossy Road’s huge success meant that Hipster Whale has fended off many potential acquirers in the last 14 years – but none of those offers had the appeal of Atari.
There have “definitely been ongoing conversations, like even since launch week,” Hall tells us. “But obviously there wasn’t ever an enticing offer…we’ve always wanted really good partners and that’s one of the reasons we’re so excited to work with Atari.”
“If you think about what that brand is and what that brand means, it’s retro, it’s a celebration of the joy of the arcade. That’s their past and what they’re doing today. I think you’ll be hard pressed to find a mobile company more aligned with that spirit.”
Hall has known Atari boss Wade Rosen for years, even before Rosen took charge of Atari and set about reviving its fortunes in 2021. They share a deep love of retro and arcade games, and the two had kept up a regular dialogue until Gamescom 2025, when the conversations got more serious. That was when the wheels for a potential acquisition started turning.
By June of this year, the deal was done for an initial $29.3m, making Hipster Whale part of a growing portfolio of Atari-owned retro or arcade game specialists that also includes Digital Eclipse and Nightdive Studios.
And so of course, the Crossy Road maker is busy delving into the Atari archives to see what makes sense to work on next. “Pong, Breakout, Centipede and Missile Command are still sort of around today, but they’re not available on mobile at the moment, so that’s what I’m interested in,” says Hall.
“I can’t wait to bring some of these classic titles back, even if they’re just preserved…but also update them and make them exciting – a modern take, even.”
Hall says that he and Rosen also share a passion for preservation, and as a result he wants Atari’s classic brands to be live and playable on every platform possible, including typical formats right through to Apple TV, Netflix and arcade cabinets.
The Hipster Whale team is already working on bringing a load of Atari properties to Crossy Road, of course, and Hall says that it would make sense for retro collections like Atari 50 to be available on mobile too.
“I think there’s just so much potential to bring across some of those beloved titles and put them on mobile and present them in fun ways. I certainly can’t promise anything’s coming, but there are some obvious moves there.”

title: King seemingly escapes major layoffs in latest round of Xbox cuts
text:
Xbox has announced the latest stage of its restructure which will see 268 jobs lost across first-party studios, XGS management and central functions.
King seems to have dodged most of the cuts, and has expanded its remit to include Microsoft Casual Games, which makes evergreen titles like Solitaire Collection, Minesweeper and Mahjong for PC and mobile.
Xbox exec Matt Booty confirmed in a blog today that the new layoffs mean the troubled division is now three quarters of the way through the restructure announced in July . As we reported a week later, King escaped most of the Xbox cuts and was effectively ‘promoted’ within the hierarchy, alongside Mojang.
Both studios will now report directly into Xbox boss Asha Sharma, it was confirmed in July. “These two studios have increasingly become platforms and are our largest by monthly active players,” Sharma said in a blog  announcing the news. “They bring critical geographic, demographic, and differentiation to Xbox.”
The cuts and reorganisation mostly hit Xbox’s first party console and PC studios. The moves mean Activision will oversee Rare, World’s Edge and develop the next Halo game. Bethesda will now absorb Obsidian, and Playground Games and Turn 10 will merge. Xbox also confirmed that Cambridge, UK-based Ninja Theory will likely close, and that Double Fine, Compulsion Games and Undead Labs have each been divested.
As we reported last week, staff at King’s Stockholm and Malmö offices are set to go on strike at 5am this Friday, September 25, after King management rejected a collective bargaining agreement that had been in negotiations for a year.
Last summer, King made around 200 job cuts , around 10% of its staff. Our sources claimed around half of those were in the Stockholm office, with 30 layoffs at King Barcelona and the rest from London, Berlin and its full-time remote workers.
Some sources claimed that some of those staff cut were effectively being   replaced by the AI tools they helped create and train .
We later reported on alleged layoff lawsuits, toxic management and low morale at the Candy Crush maker, though one insider claimed that many King staff were ‘pampered’ and overly-sensitive. In March, King refuted the claim that AI had replaced some jobs .

title: Monopoly Go reveals new KPop Demon Hunters and Ghostbusters crossovers
text:
Scopely’s blockbuster mobile game Monopoly Go is teaming up with Netflix hit KPop Demon Hunters and the Ghostbusters franchise for its next “Monster Mash” season.
Running from September 23 to November 25, the season brings Huntr/x, the Saja Boys and the Ghostbusters crew into the game through new mini-games and board experiences, including in-game use of Huntr/x’s songs Golden and How It’s Done.
KPop Demon Hunters fans will find a themed shopping boutique, a street race through Seoul that leads into the Underworld, and a Huntr/x concert experience, with the Ghostbusters crossover adding a rooftop race around 550 Central Park West and a Firehouse-set challenge built around the franchise’s Proton Blaster.
The season also introduces two new head-to-head features for players to take on friends directly – in Fill Up Your Luck-O-Lantern collected candy can be shared with another player, and Trick-or-Treat is Knocking is a dice duel where the higher roll wins goodies.
Elsewhere, a new Mystery Mansion Sticker Album adds 25 sets tied to the season, including two dedicated entirely to KPop Demon Hunters and Ghostbusters respectively.
The crossover is the latest high profile brand collaboration to be executed in Monopoly Go, following on from a Star Wars crossover event in 2025 and The Simpsons earlier this year.
The new KPop Demon Hunters and Ghostbusters season follows on from the Looney Tunes crossover currently live in Scopely’s hit mobile game.
Monopoly Go has passed 300m downloads since launch, said Scopely in today’s announcement. Sensor Tower said in January this year that Monopoly Go was the fastest game to reach $6bn in IAP revenue. It easily beat the likes of Monster Strike, Honor of Kings, Royal Match, Genshin Impact and Clash of Clans to the $6bn mark about three and a half years after its launch in April 2023.

title: 触乐怪话：花枝鼠听到自己要做肿瘤手术当然不会觉得荒谬
text:
触乐怪话，每天胡侃和游戏有关的屁事、鬼事、新鲜事。
图/不是小罗
我最近的日常基本由两部分组成：出差，和照顾老鼠。严谨一点来说，这个“照顾”的过程已经持续了很长一段时间。
我以前分享过，我养了很多只老鼠，在一个宽敞的双层横丝中西笼里。而现在明明距离上次分享好像也没有很久，但是我的老鼠已经数量减半……老鼠的寿命实在很短，但我再仔细看，发现距离我有很多老鼠的时候已经过去了很长一段时间。
大部分老鼠的寿命在2年左右，据说少部分基因出色、得到好的照料的可以活到3年以上，而我养的老鼠大部分集中在2年半这个年龄去世，因为很多时候它们年龄相似，所以有一段时间我接连送走老鼠，过程中感觉很恍惚。其中有两只老鼠死于肺部肿瘤，延缓它们生命的过程中，我在家里添置了一台医用制氧机，做了一个吸氧箱，附带各种药品无数，但是效果也不算真的很好。
我参考了这个布置，不过制氧机是鱼跃的
在各种各种老鼠中，我照顾的时间最久的老鼠是一只红眼暹罗鼠，目前已经2岁6个多月，依然非常坚强地生活着。这只鼠是被我领养回来的，来的时候1岁多，当时脖子上就带了一个小囊肿，并且在到家一周内长得非常大——所以我们认识没多久，第一件事就是带它去做手术。手术很顺利，切下来一块巨大的囊肿，肿块边缘清晰，检验结果为良性；做完手术后它依然非常活泼，当晚自己拆掉了医生绑好的鲨鱼鳍。
也是从第一次手术开始，为了方便照顾它（比如上药、绑绷带）和观察它的恢复情况，我开始让这只老鼠和我一起住。它没有一个特别明确的名字，前主人给它取了一个名字，但是当时我从前主人那里领养了4只鼠，它们的名字总被我记岔，叫起来很随机。后来第一次手术花了1200元，我干脆喊它“1200”。1200的性格非常好，有一种坚韧、坚强的美德，即使上药很痛也很配合，最多事后爬到人的手心寻求安抚。在床上居住的时候，1200甚至不咬充电线，只是喜欢偷零碎的小东西到自己的窝里。
就像这样！
我和1200度过了一段很甜蜜的时光，这段时间它恢复很快也很好，拆线时医生都感叹非常顺利。有时候夜间扔垃圾，1200和我一起出门，趴在我肩膀上左顾右盼，它性格大胆，出门时总是一副高兴的神采，有一次吸引来一只大狗围观，它也非常淡定。
大概半年以后，1200又长了一个新的肿块。
这时候1200的状态还是非常良好的，就像我前面说的，它甚至还比刚来时胖了一些，皮毛油光水滑。老鼠的肿瘤手术有点像一个对抗熵增的过程，如果老鼠状态好，切了一定更加合适。所以我立刻带它去做第二次手术。期间没有什么非常忐忑的感觉，可能是上次的结果比较安心。1200变成了2400。
2400的手术过程也可以说比较顺利，但是这次切出的肿块不再是囊肿，而是肿瘤，边缘扩散了一大块，切下来变成两节附有组织的肉。做完手术后，它神色似乎也没有上次那么好了，看起来虚弱苍白一些。医生说第二次手术的位置和第一次比较近，要小心血肿。
我继续把2400带回家里照顾。回家那天2400趴在我的肩膀上不愿意下来，当天我记得我在写一个很急的稿，写的时候它就在我的肩头哼哼唧唧。第二天睡醒起来我发现它的伤口似乎附近鼓起来一片，我不知道为什么一下子被吓到以为是血肿，哭着带老鼠赶到医院，医生说只是有点挤压到，自己会慢慢消去，我又默默地回家了……
总之，2400也再次顺利地恢复了，体重没有减少太多，依然适中圆润的一只。我开始定期给它吃一些保健品，鱼油、姜黄粉、鲨鱼软骨素、磨成粉的蒲公英绿豆金银花等等。不过不到3个月后，我领养它刚好一整年的那几天，2400又长了一个新的肿瘤，这次在乳腺位置。
实际上，到这次又新长肿瘤，我的心态已经很不一样了，这大概率意味着2400的肿瘤呈恶性，以后只会源源不断地继续长，而随着它年纪变大，做手术也会越来越困难。医生和我在医院讨论，我们都觉得它状态还非常好，或许还可以切最后一次，用开玩笑的话来说，“顺利变成3600”。可是这次切完后，它的恢复一下变得非常严重。
首先是血肿，这次手术后当天下午它就开始出现血肿，第二天医生开始给它抽血，之后一天一次抽血、打消炎药、喂美洛昔康，我没法带回家处理，于是给它办了住院手续。住院的天数一次一次续上，因为它总是恢复不好，今天血肿好像消了，明天又长出来，最后一共在医院住了半个月。整只鼠都飞快瘦下去。身价也飙升，变成了6000，其实可能更多，但是我已经不太想算了。
6000是我第一只折腾这么久的老鼠，之前的很多老鼠，虽然我同样在救治，但是很难撑到现在，也可能外部肿瘤确实能拖到时间更长。虽然这次之后，它绝对无法再承担下次手术了。出院回家后，我开始每天给它喂抑制肿瘤的药，6000精神状态又慢慢恢复，然后变得非常好，这时候我搬家了，给它换了一张更大的床，它跑上跑下。
带老鼠一直做手术的感觉很奇怪。有时候我觉得自己没有太多感觉，因为老鼠是一种肿瘤高发的动物，长了就判断情况，情况良好时切掉，不然就抑制。有时候我也觉得这个世界对老鼠真的是不公平，老鼠实在是一种让人伤心的动物。

title: 这个9月，“鸡否”成了玩家接头的新暗号
text:
■ 引言
近两年，游戏内的术语似乎有了更多语义。很多原本只在圈内使用的小众词汇成了年轻人更形象、更有意思的表达方式。“吃鸡”就是一个好例子。它早已不只是战术竞技类游戏中的胜利代名词，而是被越来越多的玩家乃至普通人活用于日常生活当中。
比如你会听到有年轻朋友说“面试吃鸡”“考试吃鸡”“比赛吃鸡”……在年轻的圈子里，大家把它作为“获得胜利、达成目标”的另一种表达方式。同时也会看到各个年龄段的人在聊天群、或社交平台上相约“吃鸡？”“吃鸡！”——这时“吃鸡”已不仅代表“胜利”，更是成为了生活中与好友一起快乐游玩的社交关键词。
像“吃鸡”这类表达在日常中的高频率使用，代表它们已经成为生长在社区中的“长青”文化符号。
7年前的一句“大吉大利，今晚吃鸡”，《和平精英》率先验证了战术竞技玩法在移动端的可行性，让“吃鸡”这个词第一次面向大众，成为当时最火的游戏代名词；时至今日，当人们聊起“吃鸡”时，大家第一个想到的也是《和平精英》。
“吃鸡”这一符号能够持续生长、在人群中获得足够的文化认同，并不是因为足够多的玩家——玩家的聚集更像是一个结果：《和平精英》通过玩法和社区文化的持续构建，最终让“吃鸡”演化成为能够不断扩圈的文化，让更多玩家被吸引、留下，并继续辐射向圈外的更多人。
这似乎成为了一个循环。《和平精英》的“吃鸡”文化借此不断发展，吸纳圈层更外围的人们。比如今年9月的“吃鸡节”就成了一个能看得见的好落点。
■ 有“鸡味”的重庆
《和平精英》的“吃鸡”文化带来的热度令人惊喜。
截至9月22日，“吃鸡节”相关话题在各大社媒共上榜热搜达38次，各种物料在线上仍在持续发散热度。
在抖音和快手的榜单中，“吃鸡”话题均居于高位
与此同时，我看到有不少玩家在社媒上分享自己的活动感受和“战利品”，在他们的发言里出现频率最高的一个词，就是“鸡否”。随帖附上的，是重庆观音桥附近人山人海的画面。
“人多”成为玩家们最直接的感受之一
9月19日，《和平精英》“吃鸡节”在重庆打造“吃鸡痛城”——超过3500余平米的观音桥圆形广场及附近商业街都被大面积覆上“吃鸡”元素。活动中巧妙地融合了重庆五一爆火的“机车夜游落地签”文化，携手4月官宣联动的“张雪机车”空降长嘉汇购物公园，打造出趣味十足的《和平精英》版“落地签”。同时，“巨型赛博三级头”空降云端之眼高空观景台，全城的大屏也都被《和平精英》点亮。游戏、城市、合作品牌通过“吃鸡”这个符号融为一体，让玩家、当地人和来往游客体验在重庆“吃鸡的一天”。
体验联动版张雪机车的玩家
520米高的“云端之眼”已经变成了“吃鸡”的模样
在这里，“吃鸡”又成了玩家打卡成功的新说法。总体来看，《和平精英》通过“吃鸡”把重庆打造成了真正意义上的“痛城”。观音桥的新地标——巨型“三级头男”雕塑和“沙丘之主”艺术雕塑；在附近还能看到活动物料被投放在3788平方米的“亚洲第一屏”上。足够大本身就是一种震撼。加上在重庆大街小巷随处可见的物料，玩家从机场落地、路人路过街区，抬头就能看到写着“鸡否”的魔性召唤。如果要打卡所有点位，真的需要逛遍全城。我能够想象到，身处其中的玩家多少会有种“排面拉满”的感觉。能做到这点，不仅是资源上的投入，也间接映射出外界对“吃鸡”文化的价值认可。
“三级头男”雕塑与人群
“沙丘之主”雕塑与人群
巨大的“鸡否”口号与重庆夜景融为一体
在社媒里，我注意到一些玩家说自己最开始也是奔着“领福利”“与‘一日店长’合影”去的，但当他们走进“吃鸡街区乐园”之后，很快就玩进去了。
很多时候，线下活动的本质是通过强有力的资源整合能力，将社区和游戏文化搬进现实世界里，形成更直观的产品影响力。标配的解法是设置好打卡点、准备足够的周边福利，以及coser和嘉宾互动等。这些内容往往负责提供“看上去还不错”的观感，但在体验部分总会让人觉得尚有可挖掘的地方。而在“吃鸡的一天”里，玩家的体验更进一步。不仅有“吃鸡店”“吃鸡社”“热力榜ShowTime”这类以和coser、嘉宾互动打卡为主的轻度体验内容；也有像“1v1吃鸡特训营”（游戏内歼灭模式PK）和“大吉大利 一起吃鸡”（四人组队骑单车游戏）这类融合了“吃鸡”文化的趣味玩法。这和《和平精英》在线上给人的感觉相似，在足够细分但又各具“鸡味”的玩法下，玩家们总能找到符合自己需求的心头好。
“吃鸡特训营”前，大量玩家伫立观战
在“吃鸡”文化的串联下，我发现能玩进去的不止玩家。在活动中央的“全明星‘鸡否’大会”上，我能明显感受到游戏里的氛围被搬到了线下。和游戏里的大多数时候一样，“吃鸡”不用非得是“严肃的竞争”。明星代言人、PEL职业选手以及生态内外的KOL齐聚。各路“鸡友”在主持人开场后争先表演整活，演绎游戏里的搞笑名场面；之后，品牌代言人宋茜、明星特种兵袁一琦作为“吃鸡社学姐”登场，和TEC.33Svan、WBG.Suk等PEL职业选手同台竞技。他们来自不同领域，但聚在一起后也不会显得生硬，反而因为“吃鸡”和玩家之间的距离被无限拉近。这或许也是这些“顶流”愿意一直和《和平精英》玩在一起的原因之一——一个受众高度重合、关系更近，且能够不断引领潮流的舞台。
夜灯初起，“全明星‘鸡否’大会”与现场人潮
我注意到，社媒上也有一些对活动感兴趣的路人，他们在最初或许无法理解“吃鸡”是什么，但当这种文化在线下展现出足够庞大的规模和普适性的趣味后，他们很快就有意愿融入进去了。很大程度上，“吃鸡的一天”再次展现出《和平精英》的跨次元文化叙事能力。其蕴含的潮流文化早已不囿于游戏本身，这为合作的城市和品牌带来了更宽广的影响力半径。
路人发帖称观音桥“温度都升了3度”
■ 让“吃鸡”走上更高的台阶
在“吃鸡节”里，《和平精英》和玩家一直在共同输出大量能够破圈的流行话题，某种程度上，我认为二者是共生共进的。这当然是《和平精英》通过“吃鸡”文化不断输出潮流影响力的体现。反过来，“吃鸡”文化在这些年里也随着《和平精英》走上了一个更高的台阶。
一般来说，一个新的潮流想要实现跨圈层的传播，过去需要不同的方面来分别做潮流文化的挖掘、推广和跨圈层传播工作。但如今来看，《和平精英》在生态内，就能让“吃鸡”文化持续生长、向外扩圈。
从“吃鸡”文化的最根本——玩法构筑的角度来说，《和平精英》中关于“吃鸡”的体验正在被持续拓展。比如在“激战金秋”版本更新后，“龙狮城”地图焕新回归。它原本是2022年的新春地图，在本次回归后地图内的舞龙、舞狮载具获得了新的升级，同时增加稻草人、柿子元素的内容，让整体更符合“金秋”的主题。对玩家来说，不论是否有情怀加持，在进入“龙狮城”地图后他们都能获得新的体验。
今年4月份，《和平精英》开启“梦中情图回归计划”，“龙狮城”获得7733万投票登顶榜首，玩家在评论区表示“必须投龙狮城”
除了“吃鸡”玩法代表的BR类玩法不断升级外，这些年《和平精英》还推出了如“地铁逃生”“超体对抗”等更多玩法，本质上是项目组在尝试找到社区和产品之间的最大公约数、发现玩家真正想要的是什么，并在此之上结合当下的流行趋势和玩家诉求，为“吃鸡”赋予更多当下流行的体验，让更多射击品类的玩家也能感受到“吃鸡”的乐趣。这也保证了在《和平精英》里，“吃鸡”带来的体验是丰富、新奇的。
在玩法之外，“吃鸡”文化的破圈也离不开《和平精英》庞大的用户池：2026年除夕时，游戏DAU突破9000万。在这样的用户规模下，社区中能孵化出足够丰富的内容生态，让“吃鸡”文化源源不断地内生出来。在此基础上，《和平精英》也提供了深厚的技术能力和极快的响应能力——这一点我们已经不止一次见识过。比如与《哪吒之魔童闹海》《蜘蛛侠：崭新之日》这类针对热点的迅速合作与落地能力。通过社区与项目之间的互相配合，才能将藏在玩家日常里的趣味内容提炼出来、再通过自上而下的引导形成潮流，经由线上线下活动的持续落地不断扩散出圈。
7月29日《蜘蛛侠：崭新之日》上映，《和平精英》官宣联动
当然，“吃鸡”文化想要拓展到更广泛的人群，光靠好玩和有梗还不够。《和平精英》也在参与更多社会性事件的过程中，实现“吃鸡”文化的持续破圈。这包括在“吃鸡节”中高调亮相的张雪机车联动；也包括即将在9月28日至29日举行的第20届亚运会电子竞技《和平精英》亚运版本项目，它作为第二次入亚、同时也是唯一一个入选的射击游戏项目，自然也受到更多来自世界各地的关注。当《和平精英》在大众视野下以更积极的形象出现，其内蕴的“吃鸡”文化也有了向更广阔圈层跳跃的支点。
《和平精英》亚运版本项目赛程日历
也正是因为有了像“吃鸡”这样的符号，当它能够陪伴玩家、不断自我演化时，玩家才能更具体地勾勒出对《和平精英》“潮流感”的具体印象。
从近两年的“刺激之夜”到更多的联动和UGC内容来看，《和平精英》早已成为一个“平台”。《和平精英》策划总监黄鑫龙先生曾经在今年5月接受媒体专访时表示：“《和平精英》是要成为一个更完整的娱乐产品……将《和平精英》打造成一个足够丰富、品质足够高的平台化产品。”
这种“平台化”的产品定位当然需要持续接入更多的新内容、新热点、新玩法。但这些来自外部的内容在进入IP生态时也需要有一个内部支点。这也要求《和平精英》持续拓展包括“吃鸡”在内的更多原生文化符号；对于“吃鸡”本身而言，在与更多潮流文化、热点内容的持续碰撞中，它也能获得更多的生长养分。这样看来，包括“吃鸡”在内的游戏文化符号，也共同构成了《和平精英》潮流标签的底座。
■ 结语
之前，我一度习惯于将产品的市场表现与“是否有爆火的梗”建立直接关联。但对《和平精英》这样的长青产品而言，它的内在逻辑显然是更加长远的——虽然“爆梗”或许仍是关系到产品数据、社区热度的重要方法论，但它并不止于如何打造几个热梗，或单纯追逐热度。
比如“叮咚鸡”“有款游戏越打越年轻”，回顾这些梗的爆火过程，我们能看到一些相似的趋势：它们首先是孵化自社区的玩家内容，随后往往会由项目组发掘，并通过一种自上而下的引导持续为其赋能——这包括外部联动、内部打造高质量内容示范等手段；最终，这些在灵光一闪中诞生的内容会生长成为带有强烈“和平”风格的文化符号，然后走向更广泛的人。
可以看出，项目组与玩家形成了某种奇妙的默契。玩家愿意相信他们“玩”出来的梗会得到应有的重视；项目组也愿意把社区的主导权交给玩家。在这种默契下，《和平精英》能够在过去、现在乃至将来持续孵化出像“吃鸡”这样的文化符号，也就并不奇怪了。

title: 长期独自做独立游戏开发，很容易陷入自我内耗，该怎么破局？
text:
长期独自做独立游戏开发，很容易陷入自我内耗，该怎么破局？
22小时前 2.4k
本文出自知乎话题“长期独自做独立游戏开发，很容易陷入自我内耗，该怎么破局？”两位开发者的回答：https://www.​zhihu.​com/​question/​2060772698318550904
作者：王子饼干   《多洛可小镇》游戏制作人
先说结论，人会迷失、会内耗的最主要的原因就是因为缺乏反馈，不管是好的反馈还是坏的反馈，反馈决定了我们该走向何处。想象一下你走在沙漠里，很容易感觉到绝望和迷茫，因为走在沙漠里就是一个没有反馈的事情，你不知道自己走到哪里了，你不知道接下来该走向何处，走到什么时候是一个头。
我经常把制作独立游戏这件事类比为走在沙漠里，和写公众号文章或者录剪视频不一样，后者是相对较短的，就像一个视频up主，做一个视频不需要做游戏那么久，做完了直接上传到目标平台就可以直接获取反馈，会有播放量、完播率、互动数量这些后台数据；也会有用户评价这类前台数据，反馈来的是非常快的。但前者正如我的比喻所说，走在沙漠里，长久看不到反馈，这就是问题所在。
所以要缓解这个问题，要做对三件事：
尽可能地缩短开发周期
这个目标其实挺复杂的，它跟很多元素都有关系，比如你的游戏规模、你的团队规模、你的开发成本、以及处理问题的经验、工具链和生产管线的先进程度等等。但最重要的一个因素就是，你的游戏本身的规模，根据你的规模来定制大小合理的游戏项目，这是重中之重。
制定严格的​RoadMap
说白了就是有一个非常完善且详细的路图，这个路图的形式可以多种多样，比如我认为一种万能的路图是，把游戏开发拆为十个大版本，0.1，0.2，0.3这样，然后我们0.1版本要做哪些功能和系统？0.2版本要做哪些等等，当然也有别的形式，而且也不一定是非要分成十个大版本。但路图非常重要，它其实就是告诉你，我走到哪里了，我接下来该怎么走，如果我没有在规定的时间内完成当初0.1版本规定的计划，是因为什么？是开发上受挫还是对低估了目标游戏系统的开发难度，不管是什么错误，它可以让你产生一个内部的反馈。
公布开发日志以及组织游戏测试
公布开发日志就类似于很多海外的独游开发者做的那样，比如在X（前推特）上的开发者大多都会把自己开发游戏的一些过程录下来然后上传到X，这样可以获得很多反馈，包括点赞数、收藏数、评论之类的信息。
组织游戏测试就是正常的找人或者找粉丝来测试游戏，比如demo版本开发完成了，或者EA版本又或者完整版本开发完成了，都可以多招募一些玩家进行测试。
________________________________________
其实我们日常感受这个世界也是因为这个世界在给我们充足的反馈，没有反馈就好像你的脚完全悬空了，它会带来很多慌乱。所以以上三件事本质上都是在寻求反馈或者加快反馈来的时间，以帮助我们快速的优化现在的游戏。
作者：Paranoia
“自己一个人用Godot做独立游戏快一年了，包揽策划、程序、美术、音效全部工作。”
一开始热情很高，每天能熬很久写代码、画素材。
从你的描述来看， 你的问题是：反馈回路断掉了。
人生是需要正反馈的，一个人闷头做事，长期没有正反馈，那么陷入内耗就是必然的。不要怀疑自己的热情，你要解决的就是怎么搭建自己的创作反馈系统。
这样的问题大部分自己做独游的开发者都会遇到。
最简单的方法，就是每周发开发分享/产品曝光，或者简单的个人思考也行，不建议发日志、频率太高了，反而影响你的正常工作。
你可以搜一下，为什么那么多独游开发者都在频繁更新自媒体？这是在 给自己搭建一个面向真实世界的反馈系统。
然后， 自媒体有一定阅读量/粉丝数后，可以尝试建群，吸纳自己的核心用户 。
然后你可以尝试把一些设计、想法在群里讨论，或者你去提问也行，这是即是在经营你的独游社群，也是建立了一个面向玩家的反馈系统。
还有就是，独游的从业者群可以加一下，里面聊聊天也能有一些正反馈的。毕竟 商业互吹虽然假，情绪价值还是有的 。

title: 七年仍在巅峰游龙，关于SLG的长期主义灵犀有了新解答
text:
七年仍在巅峰游龙，关于SLG的长期主义灵犀有了新解答
原创 作者：浔阳 22小时前 3.3k
2026年9月19日，《三国志·战略版》（以下简称三战）七周年版本上线。疯狂涌入的洪流直接将周年庆开服数量推向新高，首日开出的近百组服务器全线爆满，官方仍在增设服务器以满足玩家需求。
与之同时，游戏市场表现暴涨，三战在当天国区iOS畅销榜拿下了总榜第三、游戏榜第二的出色成绩。
这一场景，行业并不陌生。过去几年，每逢三战周年庆，服务器被挤爆、畅销榜飙升、顶级同盟高调落位、明星玩家下场喊话，几乎成了固定节目。一个上线七年的SLG，还能让玩家如若新游一样疯狂，这件事本身就值得玩味。
SLG是长线品类，这虽然是个行业固有认知，但少有人能参透真谛，维持健硕，而游戏的发展注定要有不同的思路与探索。
如今年满七岁的三战正处在下一个周期的节点上，它又一次用实打实战绩告诉外界，SLG仍有进化的空间，SLG那种无数玩家在沙盘上挥斥方遒的盛况，依旧震耳欲聋。
而数日前那场声势浩大的七周年线下庆典，或许便是这场盛况的预演。
一、三战史上首次百大同盟归位
9月12日晚，上海黄浦江畔，塔吊广场，现场竖起10米高的巨型屏幕，张飞投影在江边当阳桥怒吼，裸眼3D的效果恍若将军破壁而出，丈八蛇矛银芒乍亮，引得现场来宾心潮澎湃。
三战七周年线下庆典，用一种横刀立马、锣鼓喧天的阵仗拉开了序幕。
同日，坐落于虹口北外滩、由百年扬子江码头改建而成的国家级会场上海世界会客厅，迎来了数百名SLG核心玩家。此前，张靓颖以“2019级365区老玩家”身份担任七周年巅峰重聚圆梦官，她在视频里喊话老盟友回家。 “重聚”，成为了此次线下庆典的关键词。
三战史上首次迎来百大同盟归位，风火、炎黄、王师、花果山等数十个老牌同盟全部在列，他们或曾离开过，但三战永远记得每一位主公在游戏里趟过的峥嵘岁月。
现场旌旗林立，织锦上绣着百大同盟的名字，展区里设有一面800多份同盟名单的展示墙，上头还记录着多位玩家的故事与心声，每个名字背后莫不是三战玩家们并肩作战的回忆。
从江畔怒吼的张飞投影到被誉为“上海滩人民大会堂”的世界会客厅，三战此次周年线下庆典，委实给足了排面。官方的精心谋划、重金陈设，背后的缘由并不复杂，回馈玩家。
它是官方搭台，玩家唱主调，缺少玩家的捧场，此次巅峰重聚，无从谈起。
多名玩家便在现场吐露衷肠：他们曾在S1因抢铜矿告状结下“孽缘”，后来却成固定开荒搭子；有人替离开的盟主攒下五六十万金珠，只一句“等人回家”；玩家小短腿六级石慷慨相让，戆哒哒迁城相救，小胖团长一句“人在，就在”，给冰冷的数字资产注入温热的真情实感。
赛季会更迭，同盟会重组，霸业、土地终会翻篇，但七年积攒的羁绊不会消散，它们延伸至现实里凝结成更稳固的情谊。沙盘烽烟会暂时落幕，但兄弟还在，三战就仍有重逢的理由。
近日强势冲上抖音热榜的 #三战老玩家跨越七年赴三国之约 ，即是对此的最佳写照，无数玩家在各大社交平台、游戏社群掀起了规模宏大的“寻人启事”，公开喊话当年的老友回归，字里行间尽是玩家当年的入坑经历与热血的游戏回忆，而在这些浩瀚的重聚声音中，更涌现出许多令人动容的故事：两位玩家带着缀满同盟玩家名称的桃园结义画像，跨越山海送到大哥受众，圆了7年桃园之约； 几百号兄弟一路见证盟里的小兄弟成功步入大学名校 ，数字空间里的忘年情谊在游戏七周年际成功传递到现实中来……
这些真实的声音与故事，如同涟漪一样扩散到各个角落，抖音相关话题同时在看人数破300万，持续霸榜上海本地热榜。
从设下盛宴款待主公到玩家四处走亲访友，三战心里门清，玩家，才是游戏的核心资产。
二、开门红的S0服，藏着三战的长青秘诀
自上线以来，《三国志·战略版》便以一种横空出世的姿态牢牢占据了SLG品类的巅峰位置。七年过去，SLG赛道卷过题材、卷过画质，但三战在市场表现与玩家生态上的统治力依旧稳固。
拆解其的底层逻辑，核心就在于对玩家的极致锚定。在三战的长期主义中，游戏的高黏性不仅源于长线运营的惯性，更由两个关键归因共同支撑：畅玩保障体验，好玩驱动上限。
七周年版本推出的S0服，恰恰是对“畅玩”的回答。
步入成熟期后，任何SLG都不可避免地撞上长线运营的三个结构性矛盾：新客冷启动成本高，武将、战法、经营、攻城层层叠加，形成天然壁垒；回流用户断层明显，断档一两个赛季的老玩家，极易在硬件与节奏上被一线抛弃；新客进不来，回流融不下，游戏生态容易滑入熟人社会固化、博弈环境失活的状态。
S0服则从多个方位重塑了玩家的参与度，首先，针对新客与回流用户最恐惧的硬件门槛，S0服祭出了“千抽降门槛”与“快节奏发育”的组合拳，完成任务即享的千抽福利，直接打破了阵容冷启动的抽卡焦虑。
开服首日，世界频道便开启了狂欢模式，海量玩家纷纷晒出自己的欧皇战报，双黄、三黄比比皆是，卢植、三皇、五虎等核心橙将触手可及，让新老玩家在落地瞬间就手握战力。
与之相配的，是极致的压缩体验：全部武将次日即可升至40级，打名将爆橙装与金铢，它将传统数周的枯燥开荒压缩进48小时的“高密度正反馈”，让玩家在最短时间内找回策略手感，完成了核心乐趣的破冰。
其次，为了彻底解决“爽完即走”的留存难题，S0服精妙地打通了资产结转与账户价值的内生循环。玩家在S0服抽到的永久名将、选定的心仪武将可带入S1正式赛季，活跃玩家保底还能拿到上万金铢，这一步棋，直接将S0服从游离在主线之外的“体验服”，晋升为“S1的前置温床”。外加“双服同享，充一返二”的充值返还机制，打通了新老服的账户价值，消解回归玩家的后顾之忧。
它用“短周期、高收益、低负担”的轻量化手法，降低玩家的决策成本，玩家如同畅玩“搜打撤”游戏一样，拎着橙将和金铢进场爽快博弈，再丝滑过渡到长期生态里。
事实上，三战每年都会在玩家体验侧做文章，五周年时把广受好评的同袍小队引入S1新赛季，五人小范围社交解决前期同盟融入问题，六周年世家小团化，从300人规模缩减为50人，减轻管理负担。
做SLG的同行其实都知道玩家在沙盘博弈游戏里的比重，但鲜少人讨论，为什么这一命题每年都需要拿出来重新论证？
关键在于“玩家”这个命题的解法每年都在被环境重新洗牌。
三战运营七年，全球玩家总数超过1亿，然则2026年和2019年对比，玩家的画像、诉求、行为模式大概率发生了迁移。
三战与玩家的关系并非一次性建成的，而是需要每年校准， 随环境、技术的变化实现动态调整，如是才能维持游戏的长青运营。
此次随版本上线的军师阿志/锦儿也是对该问题的回答，他们是行业首个SLG AI军师，集合了调动、征兵、打地等多场景的“指令预约”功能，让玩家从那些高频、机械的琐碎等待中解放出来。
需知，这些游戏层面的调整与技术进阶，本质上都是为人服务，这些因轻量化、效率化而省下来的时间，最后都要作用于一个核心：玩家与玩家之间更有价值的博弈。
三、创记录的龙舆争衡，三战仍在解slg最核心的题
如何让游戏变得好玩，是三战长青的另一个归因，它同时也是无数SLG探索的命题，同行们给出了不同的路径，卷画面、卷剧本、卷数值，新晋入局者擅长品类融合，风口上的小游戏则用轻量化玩法做嫁接。
三战的解题，则始终落在“沙盘博弈生态”这一SLG最核心、最稳固的底层上。
自上线以来，三战就一直在迭代升级SLG玩法，引领品类纵深发展，如具颠覆意义的立体战场，脱离点对点直线行军的格子战，高低差的引入赋予战场更真实、更有策略的对抗，后续灵犀持续加码，引入四季更替、昼夜变换、风向变化、水战、火攻等动态变量，把一个活的三国古战场呈现在玩家面前；五周年首推的军师技，则让名将智谋与3D立体地形形成深度交互……这些进化的逻辑起点，并非炫技式的内容堆砌，而是为了充分玩家的主观能动性，提高博弈上限，撬动玩家与玩家间、同盟与同盟间的社交链。
如灵犀互娱联席总裁黎直前在此前“常青三国”论坛所言，他们选择在“单一赛道 做深、做透、做活 ”，其“所积累的方法论与用户理解远比匆匆忙忙地横向扩张更为珍贵”。
将在10月份上线的新剧本「龙舆争衡」，即是三战对SLG品类发展的又一次抢先探索。
作为SLG首个超大地图剧本，「龙舆争衡」以诛董之后的“迎奉汉献帝”为历史切口，用三个颠覆性的设计变量，来搅动SLG的沙盘格局。
第一是打破剧本常态的对手变量。 在多达4000人同服的生态里，四大联军阵营和12个势力将在三个阶段中经历两次大轮换实现动态对决，战局的不可预测性与新鲜感被再次拉长。
第二是重塑战略纵深的空间变量。
2200×2200的庞大尺寸 ，比《争洛阳》的地图面积大上一倍，它不止是单纯的物理扩容，而是伴随着12个出生州与山寨、水路、巷战的多路径解锁，让战场呈现出按阶段推进的立体纵深。
最后则是将赛季PK的胜负手从占点争霸推向动态的移动目标 ，获取最多霸业的前两名诸侯联军针对献帝展开争夺与护送，玩家需要在移动中重组防线、在运动战里捕捉动机。
「龙舆争衡」创下了三战乃至SLG多个记录，2200×2200的地图、4000+ 的玩家、12个出生州，每个数据拿出来都在颠覆行业想象。
追根溯源，「龙舆争衡」其实是 三战对GVG对抗的持续加码 。这些年三战把GVG 体验作为重要的战略聚焦 ，缘由与SLG的长线魅力息息相关，SLG本质上并非数值成长或资源积累，而是玩家群体动态博弈产生的无限可能。
合纵连横、定时集火、盟内指挥、跨盟外交，这些人与人的对抗都不是人机交互能生成的，同盟管理者、配将研究者、前线攻城手，不同类型的玩家在GVG里各司其职，老带新、集体荣誉、玩家情谊都从这些团体对抗中持续累积。
行业里不是没人看到GVG的价值， 但看到和做到之间，始终隔着一整套组织能力、规则设计和真金白银的投入 。
三战想要用「龙舆争衡」验证超大规模赛季的可行性，需要配套多个技术改进与设计调整，能让高级地产量、势力值翻倍的发展指令，回老家、支援邻州的行军加速，高自由度的推演战法，每个细微机制、规则的调整最终会相互串联，支撑超规模GVG的运转。
官方也针对「龙舆争衡」的霸业名额做分配改革，扩大到1200个，让每个活跃的玩家都能劳有所获。
站在品类的头部位置上，三战有能力来做别人不敢做、做不了、做不动的尝试，不满足于安全创新，而是承担品类试错成本。三战七年的巅峰史，其实也绝非一帆风顺，每一个革新品类的设计，都是螺旋上升的结果。
结语
此次周年庆，三战打出了“巅峰重聚，畅享新程”的口号，放在如今三战的生态里，它其实是个一体双面的互文：它既指玩家的归巢与再出发，也喻指游戏多年屹立潮头、持续迭代。
从行业观点看，SLG从来不缺后来者，但多数产品都不可避免地陷入生态下滑的终局。三战之所以敢在长线运营的深水区里，持续进行如S0服、超大规格剧本等革新生态的改动，底气来源于其多年来构建并夯实的玩家生态网络。
这便是三战对SLG长期主义的解答，人与人相互交织的真实情感纽带与社会关系，才是游戏的核心资产，他们是品类不可被数值替代、无法被AI模拟、能产生无限内容的核心。
在通往下一个周期的路上，这场由官方与亿万主公共同撑起的三国战场，仍将见证更多SLG的新征程。

title: Destiny Isn’t Dead After All, Bungie Admits It Lost Sight Of What Players Loved
text:
Bungie has admitted that it "lost sight" of what players loved about its games over the past few years, acknowledging that a series of broken promises and shifting promises caused the studio to lose the trust of its community. Now, the Destiny developer promises to refocus on its players, with plans to restore removed Destiny 2 content and evolve Marathon beyond its current extraction-shooter format.
In a new video accompanied by a blog post on the Bungie website , Bungie studio head Poria Torkan and Marathon head of product and general manager Josh Dean addressed the studio's recent struggles and outlined its plans for the future. Torkan acknowledges that Bungie's ambitions had stalled as the studio pursued too many different initiatives without enough focus on the things players actually want.
"We lost trust. We lost incredible colleagues. And our ambitions as a studio stalled," Torkan said. "We chased vision without enough focus on what players loved, and that's on us. We own that."
https://youtu.be/asnrQ1UoBQM
Bungie directly acknowledged the frustration surrounding Destiny 2--which received its last content update on June 9, 2026--including the removal of large amounts of content from the game in "sunsetting" processes.
"We haven't just heard your feedback. We understand the anger, the disappointment with us," Torkan said. "We're not asking for your trust, we know we have to earn it."
Bungie described Destiny as the foundation of the studio and stressed that it is "absolutely not done with Destiny." However, it wants to take its time with whatever comes next, starting with returning Destiny to what it describes as its original promise of mystery, discovery, and the community of Guardians facing seemingly impossible odds.
Before it shifts to new stories, Bungie plans to restore content that was previously removed from Destiny 2. That could include the Red War campaign, the Tangled Shore, or raids, including Leviathan and Crown of Sorrow. Bungie described the restoration as something that "never should have been ripped away to begin with."
Destiny 2's vaulted content will be returned to the game.
It's a notable shift for Destiny 2, which has spent years operating around the controversial vaulting of content. Bungie didn't provide a specific timetable for when the removed content will return, emphasizing that doing it properly will take time.
Bungie will also focus on the future of Marathon, where player numbers continue to dwindle. The studio plans to evolve Marathon beyond the genre constraints of an extraction shooter. Bungie's goal is to expand it into a "deeper survival experience." The studio says it wants to preserve the aspects of Marathon that players already enjoy while giving them more agency over how they play--including PvE and PvP.
Alongside its plans for Destiny and Marathon, Bungie says it has made internal changes intended to make the studio more focused. "Stability does not mean shrinking our ambition," Torkan said. "It means focusing on things that you want to see from us and making sure that our vision matches our reality."
With Bungie wanting to put players "above everything else" to rebuild the relationship between the studio and its communities, it also isn't expecting players to just accept their promises this time around. "We're not going to do it with words," Torkan said. "We're going to do it through the games that we make and how we show up for our players."
Bungie has made it clear that it has a lot to prove, but restoring Destiny 2 content that players--including me--have been longing for is a great start. But after years of promises, Bungie now has to show players that this time, it can deliver.

title: Resident Evil Director Reacts To People Who Didn’t Like The Controversial Ending, Says It Was Almost Completely Different
text:
The new Resident Evil movie from director Zach Cregger hit theaters on September 18, and it had a scary-good first weekend at the box office . The movie got great reviews but some people didn't like the ending specifically.
Cregger said in new interviews that he respects that, but doesn't agree--and the ending was almost totally different.
This story contains major spoilers.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mNd1gb19A-c
The Resident Evil movie ends by revealing that Austin Abrams' character, Bryan, becomes an infected demon after getting bitten by a child, and that the movie is actually the origin story of a monster that you might find in the games. The syringe carrying the cure to the virus shatters on the ground. In the original version, Cregger said the syringe with the cure also broke, but at that moment, Bryan simply went on a killing spree.
However, test screenings resulted in negative feedback, with people saying this was deflating and meant that the story was "over." However, Cregger told Collider that he filmed a second sequence as a Plan B, and that's the one that ended up in the movie where people root for Bryan to be cured. It led to a greater emotional journey for viewers, Cregger said, though not everyone agrees.
"I shot that shot of the scientist putting the needle in his pocket just because I had a feeling. I was like, 'I feel like I'm going to need that.' Then we were able to build a new sequence at the end. I shot a contingency of him going for the stab ... just like, if I need it, I should just get it. And thank God because that's what we ended up using," he said. "Because it keeps the stakes all the way until the end. It's like, 'Save him, save him!' Whereas before it was like, 'Kill them I guess? Kill them all?'"
In a separate interview with The New Flesh Horror Movie Podcast , Cregger said he liked the idea of Bryan reaching his "final form" as a mutant monster, especially because it's not what you'd expect.
"This whole movie wasn't this guy who saves the world. It was the origin story of a monster. It recontextualizes everything, and I like a movie that punches you in the face," he said. "I like a movie that does not give you what you want, but what it does give you is more impactful."
https://twitter.com/RENews_X/status/2102034866145726615
Some of the feedback Cregger said he received was that people enjoyed the movie up until the ending. If you're in that crowd, Cregger said he respects your opinion, but he made the movie he wanted to.
"That's too bad. I don't care. It does not bother me at all. If you don't like the ending, we just disagree. I respect it. But I would never in a million years change it."
Given how Resident Evil ended, it sure seems like there are more stories to told, and Cregger himself has said he does have sequel ideas in mind . That being said, Cregger has also said he is finished making franchise movies after getting lots of hate from fans of the Resident Evil games .
In addition to changing the ending, Cregger made other adjustments to the film based on screen tests, including removing a lot of jokes.

title: Comparing Games Like Halloween To Dead By Daylight Doesn’t Make Sense, Illfonic Says
text:
Halloween is the latest in a long line of asymmetrical multiplayer horror games to release over the past decade, and like all the others, it's faced lots of comparisons to Dead by Daylight (DBD), the decade-long leader in the genre. It's an "easy" comparison to draw, Illfonic chief creative officer Jared Gerritzen said, but ultimately it's inherently flawed.
"It's literally cricket versus baseball. It's so easy to see an image of cricket and say it's exactly like baseball; it's like, really, is it? No, it's not. Like, here are all these differences," Gerritzen told me in a Zoom call. Illfonic is no stranger to this space, having made Friday the 13th,  Predator: Hunting Grounds, Ghostbusters: Spirits Unleashed, and Killer Klowns from Outer Space all before Halloween.
"We make a game bespoke for that franchise, for that group of horror fans, and for the people who love that monster."
Gerritzen said that "others" make something more like "mixtapes," which have their own merits, but the projects are too different to directly compare, as some players do.
"And it's like, how could you not want something that is built purely for Halloween? Like, if you're a horror fan, if you're a Halloween fan, how would you just be okay with it being a secondary piece? We build things for that love of that movie, and I feel like they deserve it.
"I feel like when we choose IPs, we choose the things that we love, and that we feel could be something amazing, and it's cool that other games exist that put characters in as playable, but we don't want to make it [only] playable. We want to make it Haddonfield. We want to make it Michael [Myers]. We want to make Michael's abilities and put all these characters that were beloved into it."
Gerritzen's words hit on something I've been grappling with recently, when I tried to explain how very different DBD is from the field of bespoke, licensed, multiplayer horror games . I love DBD, but I love Halloween, and The Texas Chain Saw Massacre, and most of the others that have filled this space, too. Though there's only so much time in the day, and sometimes one game of this sort does have to beat out another for my free time, I keep them all in my rotation.
"If you're a horror fan, you should consume everything, you know?" Gerritzen added, imagining a similar sentiment in horror movies to prove how silly he thinks it sounds. "'Oh, I'm just gonna watch only movies from this director.' It's like, 'Come on. No, you're not. You're gonna watch everything.'"
As for the people who wrote Halloween's obituary before it had even been released, Gerritzen reminded players of Illfonic's track record.
"How many Illfonic-published games [have shut down]?" he asked rhetorically. The answer is none, as he confidently implied. Friday the 13th was shuttered due to a rights issue, but Illfonic didn't publish it, and it remains a unique case in this space anyway. Meanwhile, the team's other games in this genre are still running today.
Gerritzen explained how this talking point has become a refrain for players in this space, and how the team blocks out the noise.
"As soon as we started doing Predator, people were asking about it," he recalled. "Same in Ghostbusters, same in Killer Klowns, same in [Halloween], and it's like, cool. All we have to do is prove you wrong. Predator has 30-some-odd predators right now. You know, we're talking about doing some really cool stuff with that. Klowns has all this great stuff. Like, we slow things down for sure. But it's not like Illfonic has ever shut a server down [or] closed down shop. Halloween has a lot of really long legs, and we've got a lot of stuff ready, you know, and it's exciting. So we can only prove them wrong. That's literally all we can do."
Halloween: The Game is out now on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. For more from Illfonic, here's why A Nightmare on Elm Street game hasn't happened yet .

title: Here’s Why A Nightmare On Elm Street Game Hasn’t Happened In Decades
text:
With Friday the 13th, Halloween, and other horror franchises getting video game adaptations in recent years, you might wonder when it'll be Freddy Krueger's turn, but according to Illfonic, the team behind those games, the task is harder than you might think. To do it right, one aspect of the films creates a big roadblock.
"There are plenty of IPs that people are like, 'Why aren't you doing this?' and 'Why aren't you doing that?' As much as I love Elm Street, [those movies are] about these big over-the-top kills," Illfonic's chief creative officer Jared Gerritzen told me in a Zoom call. "Same with Terrifier, where it's like these big, over-the-top kills that you would expect that you would have to do [in order] to do it right. That's the most costly thing, in some cases. You'd have to do hundreds of those to build that basis. You'd have to do all these other layers, and then it just becomes like, 'Well, shit.' Like, there are all these quagmires that we can't go into, and so for us, we're very diligent about the IPs that we choose."
With Freddy's dream world seeming like a great fit for a game, I'd long envisioned Elm Street as an obvious candidate for an asymmetrical multiplayer horror game akin to Illfonic's other titles, but listening to Gerritzen speak on the pitfalls, it occurred to me that he's right.
It's hard to imagine a game creating enough elaborate set-piece kills to keep them feeling fresh for players who may play for dozens or hundreds of hours, but neither does it make sense to rinse and repeat the same standout moments like Tina's nightmare that saw her crawling on the ceiling, or the way Glen's bed swallows him whole and erupts with a geyser of blood.
Freddy doesn't usually catch up to someone and finish them off with his iconic glove in a way that maps well onto multiplayer. He makes a meal out of them, and that's hard to translate into a game built on replayability.
Gerritzen explained that his team has worked on so many games of this sort that, by now, it gives them something like a running start.
"We've been through this so much that when we start on a game, we already know what the pitfalls are. [...] And so we start off with a pretty good skeleton, and then we add those layers of the project that we love. We turn down a lot of stuff because it's just like, 'Hey, to do this, it doesn't make sense in a video game form.'"
Beyond those gameplay pitfalls, there seems to be a broader rights issue tying up the Elm Street franchise, too. Though Gerritzen didn't comment on that aspect, it's recently been reported that competing Elm Street movies may soon be in the works--one for US audiences and one for international audiences--because the ownership of the intellectual property is currently split. That sort of rights quagmire probably scares off some creators, following what happened to Friday the 13th .
Does this mean we'll never get a Freddy game? I don't think that's what Gerritzen meant, though it may mean a team other than Illfonic is the one to make it, or it could be that Illfonic finds a way to make it work in the future.
For now, the team is focused on supporting Halloween, which launched on September 8 and has surpassed a million copies sold, alongside its cabinet of other asymmetrical multiplayer games, Predator: Hunting Grounds, Ghostbusters: Spirits Unleashed, and Killer Klowns from Outer Space.
For more on the team behind Halloween, here's what Illfonic said about why comparisons to Dead by Daylight are inherently flawed .
